- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly negative (especially < -0.4) — model fails to capture downside risk or panic.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects downward.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model frequently forecasts a return to prior mean after a spike, but true price often continues trending.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Overweight recent history in short-term forecasts — model underestimates long-term trend persistence when sentiment is volatile.
- Underestimate upward momentum in late horizon (e.g., 25–30 days) when sentiment is consistently positive — model assumes trend will reverse or flatten.
- Overestimate downward momentum when sentiment is mixed or negative — model underweights bullish sentiment in bearish context.
